admission.contract: A signature-verification context accepts an input stream and dispatches a parsed plaintext packet into `proc_plaintext`.
admission.predicate: a0.hit && a1.hit && a0.time < a1.time && a0.ctx == a1.ctx && a0.input != 0 && a0.sigs_only == 1 && a1.sigs_only == 1 && a1.plaintext != 0
limitations: This binds admission to the exported signature-packet API, not to a specific CLI or fd-based caller.
The public issue names the fuzz target but the harness is out of scope, so the exact external caller is not identified from source alone.

root.contract: `proc_plaintext` preserves the same `PKT_plaintext *pt` alias across the `free_packet(pkt, NULL)` boundary, leaving a dangling plaintext pointer live in scope.
root.predicate: r0.hit && r1.hit && r0.time < r1.time && r0.pt != 0 && r1.pt == r0.pt && r1.pkt == r0.pkt && r1.sigs_only == 1
limitations: Freedness is inferred from fixed source order: `r1` is immediately after `free_packet(pkt, NULL)` on line 949.
The contract proves a dangling alias is retained in scope, not allocator metadata state.

target.contract: After freeing `pkt`, `proc_plaintext` immediately consumes the same dangling `pt` pointer in the plaintext-marker construction path.
target.predicate: t0.hit && root.r1.hit && root.r1.time < t0.time && t0.pt == root.r1.pt && t0.sigs_only == root.r1.sigs_only
limitations: The first consuming operation is the size expression `6 + pt->namelen`; later reads of `pt->mode`, `pt->name`, and `pt->timestamp` are not separately modeled.
This contract binds the dangerous use to the retained pointer identity, not to a particular allocator reuse pattern.
